evals.name: human-pr-review
evals.prompt: I have to review PR #2452 in rocketride-org/rocketride-server today (the GMI Cloud endpoint fix). Can you make me something that walks me through it so I don't have to stare at the raw diff?
evals.expected_output: A local HTML walkthrough page for #2452 with a review guide (look-first items with risk, change map), every changed line explained, reasoning labelled as from the PR text or inferred (not the author's notes), checks per behavior change, GitHub comment links, and a reading time near 10 minutes.
assertions: Produces an HTML page the user can open locally
Every file the PR changes is covered on the page
Points the reviewer to the riskiest places first, each with a reason
Says where the reasoning comes from (the author vs an inferred reading)
Links changes to their lines on GitHub so the reviewer can comment
Gives a concrete thing to check for changes that carry behavior
Readable in about 10 minutes (no more than about 2,600 open words)

evals.name: stacked-batch
evals.prompt: make pr walkthroughs for the two wave PRs #2517 and #2518 in rocketride-org/rocketride-server, the second one is built on the first
evals.expected_output: Two walkthrough pages plus an index page; #2518 is detected as stacked on #2517 and its page covers only its own commits; the index shows the stack in reading order.
assertions: Produces one HTML page per PR plus an index page
The #2518 page covers only #2518's own changes, not #2517's again
The index shows the reading order of the stack
Links changes to their lines on GitHub so the reviewer can comment
Points the reviewer to the riskiest places first, each with a reason

evals.name: local-branch
evals.prompt: before I open a PR, explain what my branch fix/RR-TBD-question-keep-indentation changes compared to develop, in a way my reviewer can follow
evals.expected_output: A walkthrough page for the local branch (no GitHub links since there is no PR), every changed line explained, a review guide, reasoning from the commit messages.
assertions: Produces an HTML page the user can open locally
Every file the branch changes is covered on the page
Points the reviewer to the riskiest places first, each with a reason
Says where the reasoning comes from (commit messages here, since there is no PR)
Does not invent a PR number or GitHub links for an unpushed branch
